final_answer:
Let \(n=p+1\). Up to similarity,
\[
\Phi=J\otimes I-I\otimes J^T
\]
has the same Jordan form as
\[
T=J\otimes I+I\otimes J,
\]
since \(J^T\sim J\) and \(-J\sim J\). Identify the underlying vector space with
\[
A=F[x,y]/(x^n,y^n),
\]
where \(T\) is multiplication by \(z=x+y\).

Put \(w=y\), so \(x=z-w\). Since \(n=p+1\) and \(\operatorname{char}F=p\),
\[
(z-w)^{p+1}=z^{p+1}-z^p w-z w^p+w^{p+1}.
\]
Because \(w^{p+1}=0\), the \(F[z]\)-module \(A\) has generators
\[
e_i=w^i,\qquad 0\le i\le p,
\]
and relations
\[
z^{p+1}e_i-z^p e_{i+1}=0\quad(0\le i\le p-1),
\]
together with the extra term \( -z e_p\) in the relation for \(i=0\), and
\[
z^{p+1}e_p=0.
\]
Equivalently, after harmless sign changes, the relation matrix has nonzero entries
\[
z^{p+1}\text{ on the diagonal},\qquad z^p\text{ on the subdiagonal},\qquad z\text{ in the corner }(p,0).
\]

Its Smith invariant exponents are determined by the minimum \(z\)-adic valuations of minors. For \(1\le k\le p-1\), a \(k\times k\) minor using the corner \(z\) and \(k-1\) subdiagonal \(z^p\)'s has valuation
\[
1+(k-1)p.
\]
For \(k=p\), the least valuation is
\[
p^2,
\]
with two lowest terms contributing coefficient \(2\ne0\) since \(p\) is odd. For \(k=p+1\), the full determinant has valuation
\[
(p+1)^2.
\]
Thus, if the Smith exponents are \(a_1\le\cdots\le a_{p+1}\), then
\[
a_1=1,\qquad a_2=\cdots=a_{p-1}=p,\qquad a_p=2p-1,\qquad a_{p+1}=2p+1.
\]

Since multiplication by \(z\) on \(F[z]/(z^a)\) is one nilpotent Jordan block of size \(a\), the Jordan form of \(\Phi\) is

\[
\boxed{
J_{2p+1}(0)\oplus J_{2p-1}(0)\oplus (p-2)J_p(0)\oplus J_1(0)
}.
\]

The block sizes sum to
\[
(2p+1)+(2p-1)+(p-2)p+1=(p+1)^2,
\]
as required.
